title: Moon base: fourteen days of night (one take, flowing script, people on the plain)
note: Nov 24, second version. One camera take, no cut and no transition effect. The picture is NASA's 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026), source frames 165-329 run there and back; night_fall.py (specs/night_v12_one.json) works on a 3510x1920 strip of it and moves a 1080x1920 frame across that strip at 1:1. New in this take: the camera tilts up into the sky during the night (sky made above the source: NASA's Deep Star Maps 2020 for the faint stars and the Milky Way, the HYG catalogue for the bright stars, both placed for the Sun at ecliptic longitude 292 degrees, mid-January: an assumed date); the Earth is redrawn with the crescent the Sun's place in NASA's own frame allows (about 3.5 % lit; NASA drew about 8 %), keeping NASA's colours; the shadow's edge follows the ground and is drawn out along the Sun's rays; an astronaut from a second NASA animation (the Moon Base November update, slowed to 0.4x by motion interpolation) stands in the foreground at the end, cut from his own shot and relit as the view requires (Sun behind him). Also ours: the night, every lamp and status light, two landers' engine lights, dust at touchdown, spacecraft and a station crossing in orbit, helmet lamps of people walking and a rover far off, the grain and lens fall-off. Credit NASA; NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio (Deep Star Maps 2020; Gaia DR2: ESA/Gaia/DPAC); star positions HYG database (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py). In this version: the narration is rewritten to flow (four passages, each synthesised in one piece) and the take is 25.0 s; the faint sky comes up only as the camera leaves the lamps; the zodiacal light is added along the ecliptic (shape modelled, strength our choice); four people on foot with shadows whose length follows the Sun's height (4.5 degrees, read from a rover's shadow in NASA's frame); spacecraft in low orbit move at about 0.2 degrees a second; a little of the view's glare lies over the astronaut.

shots.job: This shot follows one night at the base in a single take: the Sun low over the ridge as a lander comes in and the ridge's shadow crosses the base; lamps, helmet lamps and stars in the dark under a crescent Earth; first light on the high ridge and across the plain; the shadow coming back as the camera returns to the Sun and a second lander arrives. So the viewer lives through the night the sentences describe. (NASA concept animation; everything listed in the note added)

lines.say: On most of the Moon, night lasts about fourteen days. Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
A crew can't do that. Life support has to keep running, and no base has yet run through a lunar night.
text: Life support has to keep running,

lines.say: Some ridges at the south pole get sunlight most of the time, but even the best go dark for days in some seasons.
